source_audit: Bourgain–Yehudayoff, Monotone expansion, https://arxiv.org/html/1108.2555, Section2 Claim2.1 and the subsequent w0^-1 translation, read in R1785 and retained. R1786 proves the cancellation/ping-pong mechanism directly using Mathlib FreeGroup reduce/toWord, invRev, reduced-word uniqueness, CoprodI ping-pong, lift and map injectivity. The general square-family theorem assumes equal lengths, reduced doubled words, distinct words, and no inverse coincidences; its index set need not be finite. The concrete family uses ALL positive binary words of lengthL, yielding2^L squares of reduced length2L; endpoint restrictions are unnecessary for this sufficient family. Exact cardinality, rational and real freeness, denominators, matrix growth and separation are proved using the R1785 seed. An explicit mutually inverse Nielsen basis change proves preservation of freeness for any injectively indexed subfamily avoiding the base generator. Exact matrix multiplication supplies the recentering distance bound. No source packing, cardinality asymptotic or flattening theorem is assumed; no novelty claim is made for these standard combinatorial/group support results.

All positive binary words of lengthL>0 instantiate it, giving exactly2^L freely generating squares of reduced length2L. Their images in the R1785 rational/real seed are free and distinct, have common denominatorQ^(2L), entries and inverse entries bounded by N=(1+8/q)^(2L), and entry separation at leastQ^(-2L). Thus coordinate differences <=eta/(8*N) put the actual translated matrices inside B_eta. The large nearby cluster and the resulting scale/cardinality relations have not yet been constructed.
